family_history: No family history of dementia or neurological disease

social_history.occupation: Lawyer; resigned from firm 18 months ago after multiple client complaints and ethical violations
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife; adult children very concerned

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, severely disinhibited. Lacks any professional demeanor expected of a former attorney. Makes personal jokes about examiner's appearance. MMSE 22/30 — loses on attention, recall, orientation. FAB 10/18. Category fluency: 7/60s. Clock drawing severely abnormal. Frontal release signs bilaterally.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral upper extremity rigidity. 5/5 strength.
neurological_exam.additional: Compulsively straightens objects on desk during exam.

patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive disinhibition and personality change in a 56-year-old attorney.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. P. is a 56-year-old attorney referred by his wife for progressive personality changes over 2 years. A previously respected litigator known for his meticulous preparation and professional demeanor, his behavior changed markedly 2 years ago. He began making inappropriate remarks to opposing counsel and judges in court. He was reprimanded by the state bar for sharing client confidences at a cocktail party. He made sexually inappropriate comments to a paralegal and was asked to resign. At home, he has become impulsive, making major financial decisions without consultation, has started collecting dozens of identical items (has purchased 40 identical blue pens online), and eats continuously. He cannot stop watching the same 3 movies on repeat. He shows no concern about the loss of his career. Wife notes he seems emotionally flat when with grandchildren but was previously extremely close with them. No family history of dementia.

mri.impression: Severe bifrontal and anterior temporal atrophy with knife-blade pattern. Normal hippocampal volume. Posterior cortex preserved

scores.Rascovsky behavioural features present: 3 of 6 (three are required for possible behavioural-variant FTD)

findings.result: He began making inappropriate remarks to opposing counsel and judges in court.
Compulsively straightens objects on desk during exam.

findings.domain: Dysexecutive profile with relative sparing of memory and visuospatial

findings.result: MMSE 22/30 — loses on attention, recall, orientation.

clinical_assessment.impression: 3 of the six Rascovsky behavioural features are documented, against the three required for possible behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia, alongside a dysexecutive bedside profile. The diagnosis is behavioural and is made on this assessment; imaging supports it and does not substitute for it. Memory and visuospatial function are relatively spared, which is the discriminator against Alzheimer's disease and the reason a screening total alone understates the syndrome.

output.proposed: Sertraline 50 mg for compulsive and disinhibited behaviors
warnings: SSRI modestly effective for compulsive behaviors; titrate slowly
alternatives: Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime for agitation and sleep

results.title: Decision-making capacity in frontal-network neurodegenerative syndromes
results.finding: Patients with behavioural-variant frontal-network neurodegeneration often demonstrate financial and medical decision-making capacity impairment early in the disease course due to orbitofrontal dysfunction; legal instruments such as durable power of attorney and guardianship are described as appropriate clinical management considerations in the published literature

output.summary: Frontal-predominant neurodegeneration with orbitofrontal and ventromedial prefrontal dysfunction causes early impairment in financial and medical decision-making capacity. Published literature documents that capacity impairment frequently precedes formal diagnosis and may manifest as reckless financial transactions, ethical violations, and impulsive decision-making. Legal planning instruments (durable power of attorney, healthcare proxy) are described in the literature as appropriate early interventions when capacity is impaired. Guardianship may be required when capacity for autonomous decision-making is lost.

findings.result: Lacks legal and financial decision-making capacity

output.impression: Neuropsychological profile: severely impaired executive function (FAB 10/18) and social cognition (Faux Pas 4/20) with moderate retrieval-predominant memory impairment. Assessment of financial decision-making capacity reveals marked impairment in understanding, appreciation, reasoning, and expression of choice. Selective anterior-network deficit pattern with posterior cortical sparing
Severe bilateral frontotemporal hypometabolism — a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal metabolic profile. Posterior cingulate cortex and parietal metabolism preserved

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. Age-related cerebral involutional change.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic

differential.key_features: Biomarker workup needed to exclude AD.
Late-life onset and imaging finding favour neurodegeneration.
No motor neuron signs on exam.

optimal_actions.action: Consult behavioral/cognitive neurology for syndromic diagnosis, biomarker interpretation, and longitudinal care plan
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Behavioral neurology confirms bvFTD syndrome, coordinates biomarkers and disclosure

optimal_actions.action: Perform a structured behavioural and cognitive assessment with informant history, scored against the six behavioural features of the Rascovsky criteria — disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, perseverative or compulsive behaviour, dietary change, and a dysexecutive profile with relative sparing of memory and visuospatial function — and record how many are present
optimal_actions.expected_finding: At least three of the six behavioural features documented from the informant history, with a dysexecutive profile and relatively spared memory and visuospatial function

optimal_actions.action: Order comprehensive neuropsychological battery characterising executive function, social cognition, language and memory
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-executive and social-cognition deficits with relative sparing of episodic memory and visuospatial function

optimal_actions.action: Offer an FTD/ALS gene panel after pre-test genetic counselling because of young onset or a suggestive pedigree; testing remains optional
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identifies or excludes pathogenic C9orf72 / GRN / MAPT variant relevant to prognosis and cascade testing

optimal_actions.action: Order metabolic dementia panel (TSH, B12, CMP, RPR/HIV per risk) to exclude reversible mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No reversible metabolic or infectious cause of cognitive decline identified

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI with volumetric coronal T1 to assess frontal/anterior temporal atrophy and exclude alternative structural cause
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral frontal and/or anterior temporal atrophy in a lobar pattern with relative posterior sparing

optimal_actions.action: Consider FDG-PET only after clinical assessment, labs and structural imaging if the dementia subtype remains uncertain
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal and anterior-temporal dysfunction with relative posterior preservation, interpreted in clinical context

optimal_actions.action: Search medical literature for frontotemporal dementia diagnostic criteria and management
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirms Rascovsky 2011 criteria, FDG-PET evidence (Foster 2007), and management approach (Bang 2015)

tool_parameters.query: Frontotemporal dementia diagnostic criteria and management

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

critical_actions: As an attorney, immediately address professional capacity (continuing client representation, fiduciary duties) and notify employer/state bar where required.
Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
key_reasoning_points: Rascovsky bvFTD criteria are met with imaging confirmation.
Capacity for legal practice must be addressed promptly.
Mild rigidity does not warrant DaTscan.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild rigidity is common in advanced bvFTD; DaTscan is not indicated.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Required core: structured behavioural/cognitive assessment with informant, validated neuropsychological testing, targeted baseline labs, and brain MRI. Case-specific additions: optional FDG-PET; optional counselled genetic testing.
key_educational_points: Genetic testing is optional after counselling and is not required to diagnose the clinical FTD syndrome
